coreIdea: f:A→B, every input exactly one output. Injective=no-clash, Surjective=every-output-covered, Bijective=both. Counting formulas + composition rules are the two high-yield skills.

equivalence classes induced by a function, or matrices/subsets framed as functions

commonTrapsQuickList: Equal-finite-size shortcut (one-one⟺onto) does NOT apply to infinite sets
f(A∩B) ⊆ f(A)∩f(B), NOT necessarily equal (equality needs injective f)
Preimage f⁻¹ distributes over ∪ AND ∩ always — forward image only over ∪
g∘f onto ⟹ g onto (not f); g∘f one-one ⟹ f one-one (not g)
highYieldPyqLessons: Counting pattern is the biggest cluster (14/30) — drill n^m, P(n,m), and the onto inclusion-exclusion sum until automatic.
The asymmetric composition rule (which function is guaranteed one-one/onto) is a favorite exact-wording trap — memorize the direction, don't re-derive under time pressure.
